newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crudes up, MidEast firm as more buyers emerge.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes up, MidEast firm as more buyers emerge.

text.p: Middle East crude prices firmed as July trading started in earnest.
Qatar Land was sold to a European major and a south Korean refiner at QGPC -37 cents per barrel, compared to earlier July deals at QGPC -44.
A European major was also heard to have sold July Qatar Land at QGPC -40, but this was in exchange for a Gulf of Suez cargo which was ultimately sold to India through its tender.
A U.S. major confirmed buying a July Oman cargo, but denied rumours that it was done at MPM -15, saying it was part of an internal deal, rather than an outright trade.
Bangchak was heard to have bought another one million barrels of Oman from a European major at Dubai +57, but the deal could not be confirmed.
In a tender last week, Bangchak had already bought one million barrels of Oman from a shosha at Dubai +60.
Oman MPM raised its official May retroactive crude price by $1.72 to $19.25 per barrel, narrowing the Oman/Dubai differential to 70 cents.
Traders said it was too early to assess how the Oman price change would affect spot levels. But the adjustment had been expected by many traders, which could limit its impact.
The Abu Dhabi crude market was quieter, with only one Murban trade done at ADNOC -26/27, between Japanese players.
The last July Murban deal was to Bangchak at ADNOC -33.
In the Far East crude market, a quiet market prompted some sellers to be more aggressive.
Minas was rumoured offered by a shosha at ICP +15, compared to the last June trades around ICP +17.
But traders expected the heavy sweet crude market to improve as a whole, as north Asia goes into peak demand season in July. --Azlin Ahmad, Singapore (+65 870 3082)
